doc.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022

title: Wrong notes and the Kikoski band story
summary: A wrong note depends on thinking; she tells of ending a solo on E major over E flat and the band supporting it.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Okay. So what constitutes a wrong note in improvisation?
What — can you play a wrong note when you’re improvising?

Do you mean it? Well you know if you start to think that it’s not a wrong note you know. I mean of course you know you land so bad that nobody can follow you, but we played the weekend with it was Dave Kikosky on piano and Alex Claffy on bass and Steve Johnson on drums, and Randy. And on one of Randy’s tunes it started with an E flat major. So you know I played a solo and then I finished and I purposely I ended on an E major. And it was E flat major. Beautiful. Kikosky put out the funkiest chord ever and he sounded perfect. So you know, and I on purpose I kind of wanted to land on something out. And the band didn’t blink. It just went for it and it sounds the most amazing — and then Kikosky was playing after me and he started with an E major over E flat and he kept going. And it was magic. You know when you have a band like that you are allowed to kind of explore and they kind of hold you like that and even your mistakes when it’s like a total mistake, they put something behind you that makes sense that you are not mistaken. You know what I mean?
That’s terrific. There was a critic years ago, Whitney Balliet, who said, he called jazz “the sound of surprise.”
